pronunciation.approximation: Say "iphigeneia" with the stress and length implied by the scholarly restoration "Iphigeneia".
pronunciation.note: The ASCII form "iphigeneia" is a DNS compromise; the restoration "Iphigeneia" preserves the name's scholarly dignity.

domains.title: Iphigeneia
domains.subtitle: Sacrifice
domains.lead: Iphigeneia is sacrifice, winds, aulis. The name means "Mighty-born (ἶφι "by might" + γένος "birth")" and belongs to the greek tradition.

cards.name: Sacred Name

cards.name: Living Tradition
cards.desc: Honored in greek myth, cult, and cultural memory.

mythology.lead: The stories of Iphigeneia place sacrifice, winds, aulis at the center of a living mythological world.

myths.title: Origins
myths.text: Iphigeneia appears in greek tradition as sacrifice, winds, aulis. The name's meaning, "Mighty-born (ἶφι "by might" + γένος "birth")", shapes the narratives told about this figure.

myths.title: Worship and Memory
myths.text: Devotees and later tradition-keepers preserved Iphigeneia in ritual, text, and iconography, ensuring the name survived into the modern scholarly record.

lore.culturalLegacy: Iphigeneia remains a touchstone for understanding greek religion, art, and identity.
scholarlySources: Hesiod, Theogony and Works and Days.
